title: Weather and Postcards
premise: After her mother's funeral, Edmund Coldharbour returns to the shuttered family house to catalog a lifetime of silence—boxes of unopened postcards, weather journals, and photographs with one face scratched out. A stranger named Vera Anselm appears claiming the family once answered to the name 'Voss,' and that Edmund's mother was not who she said she was. As Edmund decodes the postcards' weather-coded messages, she uncovers her mother's hidden sister, a betrayal over an inheritance of identity itself, and the truth that Edmund's own name was borrowed from a dead child. In the end, Edmund must choose between preserving the Coldharbour silence or signing her mother's final letter—which names Vera—and mailing it, finally letting the family's true name be spoken.
about_author: Oscar Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging unclaimed estates and their unanswered letters. Weather and Postcards is their second novel, written in a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At the reception after her mother's funeral, Edmund deploys her practiced deflection smile on mourners until a woman named Vera Anselm says, 'You have the Voss eyes.' Edmund's composure cracks for the first time in years. Emotional beat: the safe architecture of grief begins to fail.

chapters.title: Inventory of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Alone in the Coldharbour house, Edmund begins cataloging her mother's effects: forty years of weather journals, sealed postcards never sent, and a photograph of two girls with one face gouged away. She finds her own birth certificate lists a name she doesn't recognize. Emotional beat: dread disguised as method.

chapters.title: What the Barometer Knew
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with journal excerpts. Reading her mother's weather logs, Edmund realizes entries stop abruptly every few years, resuming with different handwriting pressure—as if someone else wrote them. The barometric readings form a pattern: falling pressure before every family rupture. Emotional beat: the dead begin to speak.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Knocked Twice
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Vera returns, leaving a postcard on the porch: a 1968 image of the house, addressed to 'M. Voss.' Confronted, Vera admits she is Edmund's mother's cousin and was erased from the family after testifying against Edmund's grandfather. Emotional beat: anger at the intruder curdling into hunger for what she knows.

chapters.title: A Name Borrowed from the Drowned
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, flashback chapters interleaved. Through Vera's account and a newspaper clipping, Edmund learns the firstborn daughter, Edmunde Voss, drowned at seven—and that her parents renamed their surviving child after the dead girl. Her entire identity is a memorial she never consented to. Emotional beat: vertigo of self.

chapters.title: Postcards, Unsent
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund steams open the sealed postcards: decades of messages from Vera, returned unopened, each describing ordinary weather and ending with 'Come home.' The last one, dated three weeks before the funeral, is blank except for a single pressed violet. Emotional beat: mourning shifts from mother to the friendship her mother murdered.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The will's executor reveals a condition: Edmund inherits only if she remains 'Edmund Coldharbour, sole issue'—a legal fiction her mother constructed to bury the Voss line forever. Challenging it means contesting the will and proving Vera's claim. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as a cage with a price tag.

chapters.title: Storm Front
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A storm knocks out power; by candlelight, Edmund finds the gouged photograph's missing half hidden in the barometer case—the two sisters smiling, arms linked. She also finds her mother's unfinished letter to Vera, begun and abandoned eleven times. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through the archive of resentment.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Weather
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, climax. At the will reading, relatives demand Edmund sign the affidavit erasing the Voss name permanently. Instead she reads aloud her mother's unsent letter, then the postcards, then the truth about the drowned child. The room fractures; the executor refuses; Edmund tears the affidavit. Emotional beat: the smile abandoned forever.

chapters.title: Fair, Then Clearing
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, epilogue in spring. Edmund legally restores her name to Edmund Voss-Coldharbour, mails her mother's finished letter to Vera, and plants violets where the photograph was buried. On the porch, watching clouds break, she writes her first postcard in years—and sends it. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as choice, not sentence.
